subsystems.name: Camera array
subsystems.role: 26 small refracting telescopes stare at the same patch of sky; 24 normal cameras plus 2 fast cameras that read out quickly so the brightest stars can be observed without saturating.
parts: off-axis lens assemblies, about 120 mm aperture
mounting interface to the optical bench

subsystems.name: Focal planes
subsystems.role: turn starlight into precise brightness measurements.
parts: four large CCDs per camera — roughly a hundred in total
readout at 25 s (normal cameras) and 2.5 s (fast cameras)

subsystems.name: Optical bench and thermal control
subsystems.role: holds all 26 cameras in rigid alignment and keeps them stable to fractions of a degree over years.

subsystems.name: Onboard data handling
subsystems.role: raw images from a hundred CCDs far exceed the downlink, so windows around target stars are extracted and compressed in orbit.

subsystems.name: Service module
parts: attitude control thrusters and star trackers

subsystems.name: Ground segment
subsystems.role: operates the spacecraft and turns telemetry into light curves.

buildSteps.title: Design the optics for bright stars
buildSteps.detail: A lens telescope with no central obstruction gives a clean point-spread function and little scattered light, so the very bright stars PLATO targets can be measured accurately. Several lens materials are stacked to control colour blur across the wide passband.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate and coat the lenses
buildSteps.detail: Each lens is ground, polished to a precise aspheric figure and anti-reflection coated; stray-light baffles are fitted around the barrel.

buildSteps.title: Build the focal planes
buildSteps.detail: Thinned, back-illuminated CCDs are packaged four to a camera with their readout electronics, giving a large sensitive area and fast, low-noise readout.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the payload
buildSteps.detail: The 26 cameras are bolted to a single stiff bench in a partly overlapping pattern, then aligned so their fields of view add up to one big patch of sky.

buildSteps.title: Test on the ground
buildSteps.detail: The payload and then the whole spacecraft go through thermal-vacuum, vibration and electromagnetic testing, and the photometric performance is verified against artificial stars.

buildSteps.title: Launch to L2
buildSteps.detail: A rocket lifts the spacecraft into space; it cruises about 1.5 million km away from Earth to a stable halo orbit around the second Lagrange point, where the thermal environment is steady and the Earth never blocks the view.

buildSteps.title: Commission
buildSteps.detail: Detectors are cooled and stabilised, focus and alignment are checked, and the pointing and data pipeline are calibrated on real stars.

buildSteps.title: Run the survey
buildSteps.detail: The spacecraft stares at one patch of sky for two years, then steps to a second patch, downlinking reduced data daily and building continuous brightness records for hundreds of thousands of stars.

prerequisites.why: proved by earlier transit missions; PLATO must reach comparable precision on much brighter stars.

prerequisites.tech: Large-format CCDs with fast, low-noise readout
prerequisites.why: a hundred detectors must run simultaneously for years without drifting.
the raw image rate cannot be downlinked, so bright-star windows must be selected and compressed in orbit.

prerequisites.tech: A heavy-lift launcher and a deep-space ground network
prerequisites.why: the payload mass and the continuous data stream need both.

prerequisites.tech: Precise stellar catalogues and asteroseismology models
prerequisites.why: the same light curves are used to measure star sizes and ages, which is what makes planet radii and habitability meaningful.

pathway.milestone: payload assembled and spacecraft in final test, awaiting its launch slot
pathway.unlocks: a launch-ready observatory and a trained operations and science team.
verified photometric performance on real stars.

pathway.milestone: first long stare of two years
pathway.unlocks: a catalogue of planets including small, temperate worlds around bright, well-characterised stars.
more sky, longer baselines and a broader sample of stars.

pathway.milestone: follow-up spectroscopy of the best targets by later observatories
pathway.unlocks: masses and, for transiting planets, atmospheric measurements — turning candidates into characterised worlds.
